item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q001_histone_related_proteins","answer":"In SCOPe, the canonical eukaryotic core histones H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 are all all-alpha proteins in the histone-fold fold, a.22. They are the close histone relatives at the family level: alternative H2A/H2B/H3/H4 chains and variants can be compared within the core-histone family, where homology and nucleosome roles are the safest transfers. Archaeal histones are also histone-fold proteins in a.22 and are homologous to the eukaryotic core histones, but SCOPe separates them from the eukaryotic core-histone family; function should therefore be transferred only at the broad DNA-wrapping histone-fold level, not as a one-to-one eukaryotic nucleosome-chain assignment. A further set of non-histone proteins, including histone-fold transcription-factor subunits such as TAF/TBP-associated factors and NF-Y-like subunits, share the same SCOPe histone-fold architecture and are at most remote histone-fold superfamily/fold relatives rather than members of the core-histone family. Thus they can be valid structural templates for the three-helix histone fold and dimerization geometry, but their transcriptional roles, partners, and chromatin biology must not be inferred simply because they sit in the same SCOPe fold.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
